members.name: Robin Hale
members.role: Marta's son; had a fever last winter

members.name: Marta Hale
members.role: leads the Coldwell outlaws; a widow whose fields were taken; wants them back, or a pardon, or enough to live on
ties: hates the Tolleys who farm her fields

members.name: Aldwin Hale
members.role: Marta's widowed father-in-law; was a Coldwell farmer and still works the old garden patch behind the house
ties: father of Marta Hale's late husband
remembers the Lean Year and will not speak of the Tolleys

members.name: Kai Ostrander
members.role: a Lanternquay quay guard who deserted after the Surge; fights better than the others
ties: SECRET: sent word to his mother that he is alive

members.name: Ned Hale
members.role: Marta's brother; was a farmer; does the threatening on the road
ties: brother of Marta Hale and Agnes Fenner

members.name: Sayer Hale
members.role: Ned's wife; keeps the Coldwell kitchen and the common pot for whoever is in the house
ties: trades smoked meat quietly with a Ferncross woodcutter
fears the gate guards more than the wolves

members.name: Pell
members.role: a runaway apprentice from Josiah Crane's foundry
ties: ran away from Josiah Crane before his indenture ended

members.name: Hob Ferrier
members.role: a Coldwell man who hunted for the steading before the Lean Year and now keeps the outlaws in meat
ties: knows the woods between Coldwell and the stone road better than anyone
grudges the Tolleys for the barn they took

situations.summary: The Coldwell households have taken a share from carriers on the stone road twice by force, and Silas Pike now comes past with an escort of guards; Ned wants to meet the next cart with more men, and Marta has not yet said yes or no.

sides.Marta Hale: Knows the road share keeps them fed but that a hard robbery will bring the guards down on the houses; she has not decided what to allow and fears Ned will do it without her.
sides.Ned Hale: Believes the carriers owe them for the fields the town took, and wants to stop the next cart properly; thinks Marta has gone cautious since Robin's fever.
sides.Kai Ostrander: Will go with Ned if it comes to it but thinks a fight on the road is how people get hanged; he would rather bargain with the carters than rob them.
sides.Silas Pike: Has been robbed twice and now pays the gate-due and hates it, but he fears Marta's people more than the due; he has asked Wat Fenner for guards on the next run.
sides.Wat Fenner: Collects the due at the south gate and knows his wife's sister leads the outlaws; he will guard the cart if ordered but does not want to meet Ned on the road.

situations.summary: Robin Hale has been coughing since the spring and is thin; Marta has sent word through Sayer to Sister Elspeth at Brackenford's chapel asking for medicine, though the sisters are not supposed to treat outlaws.

sides.Marta Hale: Would beg at the gate for her son but will not be seen doing it; she trusts Elspeth and no one else in the town.
sides.Robin Hale: Is tired of lying by the fire and wants to go out with Ned; he does not understand why his mother looks at him so.
sides.Sayer Hale: Carried the word to Agnes at the inn and is afraid the guards will hear of it; she keeps the boy warm and fed and worries the winter will finish him.
sides.Sister Elspeth: Nursed the boy through his fever last winter and will come if she can, but knows the Reeve would call it aiding outlaws.
sides.Agnes Fenner: Passed the message to the chapel and fears for her place at the inn if it is known; she is Marta's sister and cannot refuse her.

situations.summary: Pell's indenture to Josiah Crane is still in force and Barnaby Quill has written to the Coldwell road asking after him; Pell has said nothing to the others about the letter, and the paper is still sewn in his coat.

sides.Pell: Holds the letter and the indenture paper and knows that if Crane's people find him he is bound back to the foundry; he is ashamed and has told no one, not even Kai.
sides.Kai Ostrander: Does not know about the letter or the paper; he has guessed Pell is hiding something from Kettlebridge and has decided not to press him.
sides.Marta Hale: Does not know about the letter; she has taken Pell in as one of her own and would be angry to learn he is still tied to Crane.

situations.summary: Hob Ferrier and Ned Hale have twice walked the edge of the old Coldwell fields and looked at the Tolleys' barn; Marta has forbidden them to touch the tenants, but Hal Tolley has seen them and has asked the Guild for a guard.

sides.Marta Hale: Hates the Tolleys farming her land but knows that harming tenants would lose her any hope of a pardon; she has told Ned and Hob to stay off the fields.
sides.Ned Hale: Thinks the barn was Coldwell's and the Tolleys are sitting in it; he obeyed Marta but has not promised to keep obeying.
sides.Hob Ferrier: Lost his own barn to the Guild's letting and would burn the Tolleys' if no one stopped him; he walks the field edge to be seen.
sides.Hal Tolley: Farms the fields on the Guild's lease and is afraid of the men in the woods; he has asked Mercy Abbot for a guard and keeps his son watching from the barn.
sides.Mercy Abbot: Holds the lease and the Tolleys' rent; she wants the fields quiet and profitable and does not want to pay for guards, but she cannot let the outlaws drive her tenants off.

situations.summary: Sayer Hale has been quietly leaving food at the woodpile of a Ferncross woodcutter's widow, and the woman has begun leaving kindling for the Coldwell kitchen in return; Ned has noticed the kindling and does not know where it comes from.

sides.Sayer Hale: Keeps the exchanges small and secret from Ned, who would mock her or worse; she is lonely in the woods and does not know yet what she wants from it.
sides.Ned Hale: Has seen the kindling and asked Sayer where it comes from; she said a pedlar, and he half believes her.
sides.Marta Hale: Has guessed something and said nothing; she is glad of anything that makes the house warmer and does not want to shame Sayer.
